title: Direct VLBI evidence for a buried AGN in the triple-merger LIRG UGC 2369S
comment: 8 pages, 4 figures, 5 tables; accepted for publication in A&A
summary: UGC 2369S is a luminous infrared galaxy (LIRG) undergoing a late-stage merger in a triple system, where the heavily obscured northern core is suspected to host an active galactic nucleus (AGN). However, severe dust and gas obscuration makes definitive confirmation challenging. We aim to provide direct observational evidence for the buried AGN through high-resolution radio imaging, while investigating the AGN accretion and feedback properties within this merger-driven gas-rich environment. We analyzed archival European VLBI Network (1.6 GHz) and Very Long Baseline Array (1.7 and 5 GHz) data of UGC 2369S. Through high-resolution imaging and visibility-domain Gaussian modeling, we characterized the morphology and intensity of its milliarcsecond-scale radio emission. A compact radio component is detected at the northern core, exhibiting high brightness temperature ($T_{\rm b}>10^7$ K) and flat radio spectrum ($α\approx -0.45$), which confirms the presence of an obscured AGN. The sub-Eddington accretion rate ($λ_{\rm Edd} \approx 2.7 \times 10^{-4}$) indicates that it falls within the radiatively inefficient accretion flow (RIAF) state. We provide direct imaging evidence for an AGN in the northern core of UGC 2369S, revealing a deeply buried, jet-emitting low-luminosity AGN (LLAGN) enshrouded by a Compton-thick gas cocoon. This demonstrates that VLBI is a uniquely effective tool for disentangling nuclear accretion and feedback processes within the heavily obscured environments of multiple-merger systems.

AI.tldr: Using VLBI (EVN and VLBA) high-resolution radio imaging, the authors confirm the presence of a deeply buried, jet-emitting low-luminosity AGN (LLAGN) in the northern core of the merging LIRG UGC 2369S, characterized by high brightness temperature, flat spectrum, and sub-Eddington accretion consistent with a radiatively inefficient accretion flow (RIAF) state.
AI.motivation: The northern core of UGC 2369S, a late-stage merger in a triple system, is suspected to host an obscured AGN, but severe dust/gas obscuration prevents definitive confirmation via traditional methods.
AI.method: Archival EVN (1.6 GHz) and VLBA (1.7 and 5 GHz) data were analyzed via high-resolution imaging and visibility-domain Gaussian modeling to characterize milliarcsecond-scale radio morphology and intensity.
AI.result: A compact radio component at the northern core shows high brightness temperature (T_b > 10^7 K) and flat radio spectrum (α ≈ -0.45), confirming an obscured AGN. The sub-Eddington accretion rate (λ_Edd ≈ 2.7 × 10^{-4}) places it in the RIAF regime.
AI.conclusion: VLBI is a uniquely effective tool for revealing heavily obscured nuclear accretion and feedback processes in multiple-merger systems, as demonstrated by the detection of a deeply buried, jet-emitting LLAGN enshrouded by a Compton-thick gas cocoon.

title: Exploring the Milky Way stellar disk. Carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, sulphur, potassium, and copper abundances for 714 F and G dwarf stars in the solar neighbourhood
comment: Submitted to A&A
summary: [ABRIDGED] We aim to determine abundances of carbon, nitrogen, sulphur, potassium, and copper for 714 nearby F and G dwarf and subgiant stars, and to re-derive oxygen abundances using updated corrections for departures from the assumption of local thermodynamic equilibrium. These elements extend the chemical inventory of our previous studies and provide new constraints on the relative enrichment histories of the Galactic thin and thick disks. The alpha-element behaviour of oxygen is confirmed, with old stars defining an enhanced sequence relative to young stars. Sulphur closely follows oxygen, while potassium shows broadly alpha-like behaviour in [K/Fe] but residual trends relative to oxygen. Carbon and nitrogen show only modest separation in [X/Fe], but much clearer population differences in [X/O]. Copper displays a strong metallicity dependence and clear separation between old and young populations when compared to oxygen. We also find that [O/Mg] is not constant, demonstrating that oxygen and magnesium provide complementary rather than interchangeable reference scales. Quantitative comparisons of all elements analysed in our studies show that carbon, oxygen, sulphur, and potassium rank among the most age-sensitive abundance ratios in the sample and provide strong discrimination between old and young disk populations. The new abundance measurements substantially expand the diagnostic power of this local stellar sample. The results show that abundance ratios relative to oxygen, together with precise stellar ages, reveal population differences that are partly hidden in traditional [X/Fe] trends. The expanded abundance inventory provides a homogeneous reference dataset for studies of Galactic chemical evolution, Galactic archaeology, and large spectroscopic surveys.

AI.tldr: Abundances of C, N, S, K, and Cu are measured for 714 F/G dwarf and subgiant stars, with updated oxygen abundances. Elemental trends reveal distinctions between Galactic thin and thick disk populations, with O, S, C, and K identified as highly age-sensitive abundance ratios. [X/O] ratios better discriminate populations than traditional [X/Fe] ratios.
AI.motivation: To extend the chemical inventory of nearby F/G stars beyond previous studies, and to provide new constraints on the enrichment histories of the Galactic thin and thick disks by measuring C, N, S, K, and Cu alongside re-derived oxygen abundances.
AI.method: Abundances of C, N, S, K, and Cu were determined for 714 F and G dwarf and subgiant stars. Oxygen abundances were re-derived using updated corrections for departures from local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE).
AI.result: Oxygen shows alpha-element behaviour (enhanced in old stars). Sulphur follows oxygen closely. Potassium exhibits broadly alpha-like [K/Fe] but residual trends relative to oxygen. Carbon and nitrogen show modest [X/Fe] separation but clearer population differences in [X/O]. Copper shows strong metallicity dependence and clear old/young separation in [Cu/O]. [O/Mg] is not constant; O and Mg are complementary. C, O, S, and K rank among the most age-sensitive abundance ratios.
AI.conclusion: Abundance ratios relative to oxygen, combined with precise stellar ages, reveal population differences hidden in traditional [X/Fe] trends. The expanded homogeneous dataset supports Galactic chemical evolution and archaeological studies.

title: Cosmic Magnetism Science with the SKA
comment: Published in Advancing Astrophysics with the SKA II (AASKAII), 2026 (arXiv:2606.20366). Report-no:AASKAII/Vernstrom01 . Advancing Astrophysics with the SKA II (AASKAII) outlines the transformative scientific advances that will be enabled by the SKA telescopes
summary: Magnetic fields are a fundamental component of astrophysical systems, yet many key questions about their origin, amplification, and role in structure formation and evolution remain unresolved. The SKA will mark a transformational step forward in addressing these questions, enabling studies of cosmic magnetism across a large range of spatial scales and environments. This overview summarizes the main science cases in the Cosmic Magnetism Science Working Group, which cover a huge breadth of scales from the smallest scales governing planet and star formation, all the way up to the large-scale structure of the Universe. The chapter summarizes the main observational techniques for studying magnetic fields, including direct polarization imaging, Faraday rotation, rotation-measure grids, and Zeeman splitting. We also address fundamental considerations of these studies including SKA-Low vs SKA-Mid and wide-area vs deep observing strategies.

AI.tldr: This paper outlines how the SKA telescope will revolutionize the study of cosmic magnetism across all scales (from star formation to the large-scale structure of the Universe) by summarizing key science cases, observational techniques (polarization imaging, Faraday rotation, RM grids, Zeeman splitting), and strategic considerations (SKA-Low vs SKA-Mid, wide-area vs deep surveys).
AI.motivation: Magnetic fields are fundamental to astrophysical systems, but many key questions about their origin, amplification, and role in structure formation and evolution remain unresolved. The SKA represents a transformational step forward in addressing these open questions.
AI.method: The paper summarizes the main science cases from the Cosmic Magnetism Science Working Group and outlines observational techniques including direct polarization imaging, Faraday rotation, rotation-measure grids, and Zeeman splitting, along with strategic considerations such as SKA-Low vs SKA-Mid and wide-area vs deep observing strategies.
AI.result: The SKA will enable studies of cosmic magnetism across a huge range of spatial scales and environments, from planet and star formation to the large-scale structure of the Universe.
AI.conclusion: The SKA will mark a transformational step forward in addressing unresolved questions about cosmic magnetism, covering scales from the smallest (planet/star formation) to the largest (large-scale structure).

title: Exploring the synergies of $[\mathrm{O\,II}]λ3727$ with MUSE spectroscopy in PHANGS H II regions
comment: 18 pages, 11 figures
summary: Spatially resolved maps of gas-phase metallicity provide key constraints on the chemical enrichment and mixing processes that drive galaxy evolution, but measurements based only on strong lines remain highly uncertain and dependent on emission-line coverage. In this work, we present a joint analysis of SITELLE observations, covering the $[O II]λ\lambda3726,3729$ doublet, with PHANGS-MUSE spectroscopy covering 4800-9300 Angstroms, including $Hβ$, $[O III]\lambda4959,5007$, $[N II]\lambda6584$, $Hα$, $[S II]λ\lambda6716,6731$, and $[S III]\lambda9069$, within five nearby spiral galaxies. By combining these data, we construct a homogeneous catalog of emission-line fluxes for 604 ionized nebulae, 556 of which are classified as H II regions. This enables a comparison of eight widely used strong-line metallicity calibrations, five new strong-line calibrations, and an investigation of ionization-parameter diagnostics. We recover known systematic offsets among calibrations, but also find that many exhibit very low scatter, less than 0.03-0.04 dex, in radial metallicity gradients. We find that $[S III]/[S II]$ exhibits minimal secondary dependence on metallicity or extinction, suggesting that it may be a more robust tracer of ionization parameter than $[O III]/[O II]$. No significant outliers are identified in O/H or N/O within the sampled regions, indicating internally consistent abundance trends across the inner disks probed by our data. We provide a publicly available catalog of all measured emission-line fluxes, designed to support future investigations, including temperature modeling and strong-line abundance calibrations.

It compares eight widely used and five new strong-line metallicity calibrations, finding systematic offsets but very low scatter (<0.04 dex) in radial metallicity gradients. [S III]/[S II] is identified as a more robust ionization parameter tracer than [O III]/[O II]. A public catalog is released for future studies.
AI.motivation: Spatially resolved gas-phase metallicity maps are crucial for understanding chemical enrichment and mixing in galaxy evolution, but measurements based on strong lines alone remain highly uncertain and dependent on emission-line coverage. The paper aims to reduce these uncertainties by combining complementary spectroscopic datasets.
AI.method: Joint analysis of SITELLE observations ([O II] doublet) and PHANGS-MUSE spectroscopy (4800-9300 Å, covering Hβ, [O III], [N II], Hα, [S II], [S III]) for five nearby spiral galaxies. A homogeneous catalog of emission-line fluxes for 604 ionized nebulae (556 H II regions) is constructed, enabling comparison of eight widely used and five new strong-line metallicity calibrations, plus ionization-parameter diagnostics.
AI.result: Known systematic offsets among calibrations are recovered, but many exhibit very low scatter (<0.03-0.04 dex) in radial metallicity gradients. [S III]/[S II] shows minimal secondary dependence on metallicity or extinction, making it a more robust ionization parameter tracer than [O III]/[O II]. No significant outliers in O/H or N/O are found across the sampled regions.
AI.conclusion: The combined SITELLE+PHANGS-MUSE dataset enables robust strong-line metallicity calibration comparisons. [S III]/[S II] is recommended as a superior ionization parameter diagnostic. The publicly available catalog supports future temperature modeling and strong-line abundance calibration efforts.

title: Optically Selected Superthin Galaxies Remain Thin in the Near-infrared
comment: 15 pages, 14 figures, submitted to MNRAS
summary: We investigate whether galaxies identified as superthin in optical images remain superthin in the near-infrared (NIR), and how their extreme disk morphology is related to environment. From a nearby volume-limited sample, we select 210 superthin galaxies using two-dimensional bulge/disk decomposition of SDSS $r$-band images, requiring the disk component to have a major-to-minor axis ratio $a/b>9$. We measure disk shapes from SDSS $griz$ to UKIDSS $JHK$ bands. Both the major- and minor-axis scales decrease from the optical to the NIR, reaching $\sim0.6$ of their $r$-band values in the $K$ band, but the disk axis ratio remains nearly unchanged. Thus, optically selected superthin galaxies remain superthin in the NIR, implying that the old stellar populations traced by NIR light do not form a prominent thick disk. Reanalysis of our sample and a previous superthin sample shows that earlier reported NIR thickening is mainly due to a magnitude- and band-dependent bias in one-dimensional fitting. We further compare their environments with matched control samples using projected cross-correlations, reconstructed local overdensities, and large-scale-structure classifications. Superthin galaxies show lower clustering on $\sim0.1$--$1\,h^{-1}\,\mathrm{Mpc}$ scales and lower overdensities at $1\,h^{-1}\,\mathrm{Mpc}$, but no clear residual dependence on large-scale-structure type. These results suggest that superthin galaxies are preferentially central galaxies in relatively low-mass dark matter halos, consistent with a picture in which high host-halo spin helps build and preserve extended, vertically thin stellar disks.

AI.tldr: Optically selected superthin galaxies remain superthin in the NIR; their extreme thinness is not due to a bias in 1D fitting; they reside in lower-mass, high-spin dark matter halos as central galaxies.
AI.motivation: To test whether superthin galaxies identified in optical bands retain their extreme disk thinness in the NIR, and to understand the relationship between their unique morphology and environment.
AI.method: Selected 210 superthin galaxies (disk axis ratio a/b > 9) via 2D bulge/disk decomposition of SDSS r-band images from a nearby volume-limited sample. Measured disk shapes across SDSS griz and UKIDSS JHK bands. Analyzed environmental properties using projected cross-correlations, local overdensities, and large-scale-structure classifications, compared with matched control samples.
AI.result: Both major- and minor-axis scales decrease from optical to NIR (~0.6 of r-band in K-band), but disk axis ratio remains nearly unchanged. Earlier reported NIR thickening is due to magnitude- and band-dependent bias in 1D fitting. Superthin galaxies show lower clustering on ~0.1–1 h⁻¹ Mpc scales and lower overdensities at 1 h⁻¹ Mpc, with no strong dependence on large-scale-structure type.
AI.conclusion: Optically selected superthin galaxies remain superthin in the NIR, indicating the old stellar population does not form a prominent thick disk. Their environment suggests they are central galaxies in relatively low-mass dark matter halos, supporting a scenario where high host-halo spin contributes to building and preserving extended, vertically thin stellar disks.

title: Dissecting the 3D chemo-dynamical structures of NGC 1381: a galaxy hosting an ancient slow bar with an accreted bulge and thick disc
comment: 19 pages, 20 figures
summary: We applied the barred population-orbit superposition method developed in \citet{Jin2025a,Jin2025b} to construct 3D chemo-dynamical models for the barred S0 galaxy NGC~1381 in the Fornax cluster. Based on the stellar orbits in the models, we decomposed NGC~1381 into six components: (1) a dynamically warm nuclear disc with $f_{\rm nucl}\sim5\%$; (2) a rigidly rotating, BP/X-shaped bar with $f_{\rm bar}\sim30\%$; (3) a dynamically hot, spheroidal bulge with $f_{\rm bulge}\sim17\%$; (4) a dynamically cold thin disc with $f_{\rm thin}\sim28\%$; (5) a vertically extended thick disc with $f_{\rm thick}\sim16\%$; and (6) a dynamically hot, spatially diffuse stellar halo with $f_{\rm halo}\sim5\%$. The nuclear disc, bar, and thin disc are metal-rich ($[Z/\rm H]\gtrsim0$), $α$-poor ($\rm[Mg/Fe]\lesssim0.2$), and old ($\sim13\rm\,Gyr$), corresponding to in situ formation in the early Universe. The bulge, thick disc, and stellar halo are metal-poor ($[Z/\rm H]\lesssim0$), $α$-rich ($\rm[Mg/Fe]\gtrsim0.2$), and younger than or comparable in age to the in situ components, suggesting their relations with ex situ formation contributed by minor mergers. The flat metallicity and [Mg/Fe] gradients in the thick disc and stellar halo indicate they are dominated by a similar population of ex situ stars. In contrast, the bulge exhibits a negative metallicity gradient ($\nabla[Z/\rm H]_{bulge}<0$) pointing to a more complex formation history: the bulge could be either predominantly ex situ or contain a non-negligible mixture of in situ and ex situ stars. Our modelling also reveals the presence of a slow bar ($\mathcal{R}=2.40_{-0.27}^{+0.54}$), with a bar pattern speed of $\rmΩ_p=34_{-7}^{+4}\,km\,s^{-1}\,kpc^{-1}$, a bar length of $R_{\rm bar}=2.24_{-0.22}^{+0.43}\rm\,kpc$, and a corotation radius of $R_{\rm CR}=5.38_{-0.28}^{+1.59}\rm\,kpc$, which is consistent with its ancient formation time.

AI.tldr: This paper applies a barred population-orbit superposition method to construct 3D chemo-dynamical models for the barred S0 galaxy NGC 1381, decomposing it into six stellar components (nuclear disc, bar, bulge, thin disc, thick disc, stellar halo) with distinct chemical and dynamical properties, revealing a slow bar pattern speed consistent with ancient formation, and distinguishing in situ vs. ex situ formation histories.
AI.motivation: To understand the formation and evolution of barred S0 galaxies by constructing detailed 3D chemo-dynamical models of NGC 1381, decomposing it into multiple stellar components with distinct formation origins (in situ vs. ex situ), and measuring the bar's dynamical properties to constrain its formation time.
AI.method: Barred population-orbit superposition method (developed in Jin+2025a,b) applied to construct 3D chemo-dynamical models, using stellar orbits to decompose the galaxy into six components based on dynamics and chemistry, and measuring bar pattern speed, length, and corotation radius.
AI.result: Six components identified with distinct mass fractions: nuclear disc (5%), bar (30%), bulge (17%), thin disc (28%), thick disc (16%), stellar halo (5%). In situ components (nuclear disc, bar, thin disc) are metal-rich, α-poor, old (~13 Gyr). Ex situ components (bulge, thick disc, halo) are metal-poor, α-rich. The bar is slow (pattern speed Ωp=34 km/s/kpc, R=2.4), with R_bar=2.24 kpc, R_CR=5.38 kpc. Negative metallicity gradient in bulge suggests complex formation.
AI.conclusion: NGC 1381's stellar populations clearly separate into in situ (metal-rich, α-poor, old) and ex situ (metal-poor, α-rich) components, with the bulge showing evidence of a mixed or predominantly ex situ origin. The slow bar is consistent with ancient formation, supporting early assembly of this Fornax cluster S0 galaxy.

title: Evolution of Chemistry in the envelope of HOt corinoS (ECHOS). III. Sulphur chemistry in the Class 0 objects HH 212 and NGC 1333 IRAS 4A
comment: 23 pages, 17 figures. Accepted for publication in A&A
summary: Our goal is to find chemical diagnostics to determine the physical conditions in protostellar envelopes and help establish the development of matter during the formation of a low-mass star, as well as investigating a possible variation of sulphur depletion during the star formation process at the scale of the cold envelope. With observations with the Yebes-40m and IRAM-30m telescopes, we estimate column densities of sulphur-bearing species in the Class 0 objects HH212 and NGC1333 IRAS4A. A neural emulator of the chemical code Nautilus is used to constrain the chemical time, density, gas temperature, cosmic ray ionization rate, and sulphur elemental abundance in the cold envelope of these objects. We compare the resulting abundances of these species with those towards the Class 0 object B335. While sulphur-bearing species containing carbon chains are between 3 and 7 times more abundant in B335 than in the other two objects, sulphur oxides and nitrogen-bearing species are 3 times more abundant in NGC1333 IRAS4A. Our chemical modelling shows that, while the chemistry of HH212 and NGC1333 IRAS4A is well reproduced considering a gas temperature of 25 K and a sulphur depletion of a factor of 100 in their envelopes, significant differences are found in their average density and cosmic ray ionization rate. Comparing with similar studies in pre-stellar and protostellar cores, we derive an increase in the SO/CS and SO$_2$/C$_2$S ratios of about two orders of magnitude and a potential decrease in the HCS$^+$/CS ratio of a factor of 10 in the transition from the pre-stellar to the Class 0 phase. Sulphur compounds are good evolutionary tracers of the pre- to protostellar phase transition, with oxygen-bearing species being more abundant than those containing carbon in the evolved sources. Nonetheless, sulphur depletion in the cold envelope of Class 0 objects remains similar to that in starless cores.

AI.tldr: This paper uses chemical diagnostics (sulphur-bearing species) observed with Yebes-40m and IRAM-30m telescopes toward Class 0 protostars HH212 and NGC1333 IRAS4A, combined with a neural emulator of the Nautilus chemical code, to constrain physical conditions (chemical time, density, temperature, cosmic ray ionization rate, sulphur depletion) in their cold envelopes. Comparing with B335 and pre-stellar cores, the study finds that SO/CS and SO₂/C₂S ratios increase ~100× while HCS⁺/CS decreases ~10× from pre-stellar to Class 0 phase, making sulphur compounds effective evolutionary tracers, though sulphur depletion remains similar to starless cores.
AI.motivation: To find chemical diagnostics that determine physical conditions in protostellar envelopes and investigate the variation of sulphur depletion during low-mass star formation at the cold envelope scale.
AI.method: Observation of sulphur-bearing species with Yebes-40m and IRAM-30m telescopes toward Class 0 objects HH212 and NGC1333 IRAS4A; column density estimation; application of a neural emulator of the Nautilus chemical code to constrain chemical time, density, temperature, cosmic ray ionization rate, and sulphur elemental abundance; comparison with Class 0 object B335 and pre-stellar/protostellar cores.
AI.result: Sulphur carbon-chain species are 3–7× more abundant in B335 than in HH212 and NGC1333 IRAS4A, while sulphur oxides and nitrogen-bearing species are ~3× more abundant in NGC1333 IRAS4A. Chemistry of HH212 and NGC1333 IRAS4A is reproduced with T_gas=25 K and sulphur depletion factor ~100, but average density and cosmic ray ionization rate differ significantly. SO/CS and SO₂/C₂S ratios increase by ~2 orders of magnitude, and HCS⁺/CS ratio decreases by ~1 order of magnitude from pre-stellar to Class 0 phase.
AI.conclusion: Sulphur compounds are good evolutionary tracers of the pre-stellar to protostellar phase transition; oxygen-bearing sulphur species become more abundant than carbon-bearing ones in evolved sources; however, sulphur depletion in Class 0 cold envelopes remains similar to that in starless cores.

title: Kolmogorov turbulence across multi-fractal gas in Polaris Flare
comment: submitted
summary: We reveal a pristine, scale-invariant 3D Kolmogorov velocity cascade ($α_V^{\mathrm{3D}} \sim 2/3$) spanning $0.05$--$20$~pc in the Polaris Flare using \texttt{PPCOS} $^{12}\text{CO}$ data. A transition scale at $\sim 0.5$~pc marks a bifurcation in the structure functions' exponents, below which the degree of intermittency is also saturated. By deriving an analytical mapping relation ($α_V^{\mathrm{3D}}=α_V-\frac{1}{3}α_I$), we obtain the scale-invariant value of $α_V^{\mathrm{3D}}$, proving that the apparent transition stems from geometric projection and a changing density fractal dimension rather than a turbulent mode shift. Kolmogorov turbulence is smoothly inherited from the large-scale cold neutral medium, remaining uninterrupted by compression or gravity below 0.1 pc.

AI.tldr: Using PPCOS ¹²CO data, the paper reveals a scale-invariant 3D Kolmogorov velocity cascade (α_V³ᴰ ~ 2/3) from 0.05–20 pc in the Polaris Flare, with a transition at ~0.5 pc where intermittency saturates. An analytical mapping (α_V³ᴰ = α_V − ⅓α_I) shows the transition is due to geometric projection and changing density fractal dimension, not a turbulent mode shift. Kolmogorov turbulence persists from the large-scale cold neutral medium down to <0.1 pc unaffected by compression or gravity.
AI.motivation: To understand whether the observed transition in structure function exponents in molecular clouds represents a fundamental change in turbulence physics (e.g., mode shift) or is merely a projection/geometry effect, and to determine the true nature of the 3D velocity cascade.
AI.method: Analysis of PPCOS ¹²CO data of the Polaris Flare; computation of structure functions' exponents; derivation of analytical mapping relation α_V³ᴰ = α_V − ⅓α_I linking observed and 3D velocity exponents via density intermittency exponent α_I.
AI.result: A pristine scale-invariant 3D Kolmogorov cascade (α_V³ᴰ ~ 2/3) spans 0.05–20 pc. A transition at ~0.5 pc shows saturated intermittency below that scale. The analytical mapping proves the apparent transition arises from geometric projection and a changing density fractal dimension, not a turbulent mode shift. Kolmogorov turbulence is inherited from the cold neutral medium and remains uninterrupted below 0.1 pc.
AI.conclusion: The observed transition in molecular cloud turbulence is a projection effect; the underlying 3D velocity field remains Kolmogorov and scale-invariant, with no change in turbulent physics even at small scales where compression and gravity might be expected to dominate.

title: Spatially resolved optical and mid-infrared spectroscopy of SDSS1335+0728: implications for the origin of the Ansky event
comment: Submitted to A&A
summary: The galaxy SDSS1335+0728 brightened abruptly in December 2019 (the Ansky event) and has since been confirmed as the host of extreme X-ray quasi-periodic eruptions (QPEs) of debated origin. We constrain the origin of its transient activity by characterising the galaxy properties and nuclear accretion history with spatially resolved VLT/MUSE and JWST MIRI/MRS spectroscopy. We extract stellar and gas kinematics and emission-line fluxes, construct emission-line ionisation diagnostic maps, reconstruct the nuclear ionisation history via a Balmer-line light-echo analysis, and measure the mid-infrared silicate feature strength. The stellar kinematics reveal two counter-rotating stellar regions and kinematically cold gas ($σ_{\rm gas} \lesssim 60$ km s$^{-1}$), consistent with a past minor merger. Stellar populations show an old host with ongoing star formation confined to a ring at intermediate radii. Ionisation diagnostics reveal a three-zone structure: a central region powered by SMBH accretion, where high-ionisation coronal lines ([NeVI]$\lambda7.65μ$m, [NeV]$\lambda14.32μ$m, [OIV]$\lambda25.89μ$m) are confined, a star-forming ring, and a LINER-like outer region. A Balmer-line light-echo analysis yields a minimum ionising luminosity $\log L_{\rm ion,min} \approx 40.5$ erg s$^{-1}$ sustained over at least $\sim 1\,500$ yr. Broad silicate emission at 9.7 and 18$μ$m indicates optically thin dust, inconsistent with a classical active galactic nucleus (AGN) dusty torus. The data are consistent with two scenarios for the pre-2019 accretion: a persisting or gradually fading low-luminosity AGN, or a long-lived tidal disruption event (TDE) remnant disc. In both, Ansky corresponds to a slow, faint transient in a $\sim\!10^6\,M_{\odot}$ SMBH with already ongoing accretion, challenging the "faded AGN" interpretation proposed for some QPE hosts.

AI.tldr: SDSS1335+0728 experienced a sudden brightening in Dec 2019 (Ansky event) and hosts extreme X-ray QPEs. Analysis of VLT/MUSE and JWST MIRI/MRS data reveals counter-rotating stellar kinematics suggesting a past minor merger, a three-zone ionisation structure (central SMBH accretion, star-forming ring, LINER-like outer region), and a minimum ~1500-year sustained ionising luminosity. Broad silicate emission indicates optically thin dust, inconsistent with a classical AGN torus. The pre-2019 accretion is consistent with either a low-luminosity AGN or a long-lived TDE remnant disc, with Ansky being a slow, faint transient in an already-accreting ~10^6 M☉ SMBH.
AI.motivation: To constrain the origin of the transient activity (Ansky event and QPEs) in SDSS1335+0728 by characterising its host galaxy properties and nuclear accretion history.
AI.method: Spatially resolved VLT/MUSE and JWST MIRI/MRS spectroscopy; stellar and gas kinematics; emission-line flux mapping; ionisation diagnostic diagrams; Balmer-line light-echo analysis; mid-infrared silicate feature measurements.
AI.result: Counter-rotating stellar regions and cold gas indicate a past minor merger. A three-zone ionisation structure is identified. The Balmer light-echo analysis shows sustained ionising luminosity ~10^40.5 erg/s over ~1500 yr. Broad silicate emission at 9.7 and 18 μm indicates optically thin dust, not a torus.
AI.conclusion: The pre-2019 accretion state could be a persisting/fading low-luminosity AGN or a long-lived TDE remnant disc. The Ansky event is a slow, faint transient in an already-accreting ~10^6 M☉ SMBH, challenging the "faded AGN" interpretation for some QPE hosts.

title: Projection-Enhanced Disk Breaks: Evidence from Deep Photometric Decomposition
comment: 29 pages, 21 figures; Accepted to the special issue "Unveiling the Structural Properties of Galaxies Using Contemporary Wide-Field Surveys" in MDPI Galaxies
summary: Radial brightness profiles of disk galaxies often exhibit so-called breaks -- locations where their exponential-scale length abruptly changes. Some galaxies have downbending (Type II) breaks, where their brightness decays faster in outer regions, while other have upbending (Type III) breaks, resulting in more extended outer disks or envelopes. Disk radial profiles without any breaks (Type I) appear to constitute a minority. The exact fractions of different break types depend on many galactic parameters -- such as Hubble type, stellar mass, spatial environment, and bar presence -- and vary significantly across different studies. Another source of discrepancy is the orientation of galaxies: projection effects may play an important role in break detectability. In this work, we utilize DESI Legacy DR10 imaging to perform photometric decomposition of a sample of 375 edge-on galaxies and investigate their radial breaks. We find that the vast majority (~90%) of disks in our sample have Type II breaks, which is a considerably higher fraction than in many previous works (~50%). We carefully tested our results to check if observed breaks can be a result of flaring or two-disk composition. We showed that a high fraction of Type II breaks can be attributed to projection effects, which enhance the observed surface brightness of breaks in edge-on galaxies.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes radial brightness breaks in 375 edge-on galaxies using DESI Legacy DR10 imaging, finding ~90% have Type II (downbending) breaks—a much higher fraction than previous studies (~50%). The authors attribute this to projection effects enhancing break detectability in edge-on orientations.
AI.motivation: To resolve discrepancies in reported fractions of different break types (Type I, II, III) in disk galaxies, which vary significantly across studies due to dependencies on Hubble type, stellar mass, environment, bar presence, and projection effects.
AI.method: Photometric decomposition of 375 edge-on galaxies using DESI Legacy DR10 imaging, with careful testing to distinguish breaks from flaring or two-disk composition and to assess the impact of projection effects.
AI.result: ~90% of edge-on galaxies exhibit Type II (downbending) breaks, significantly higher than the ~50% reported in many prior works. Projection effects are shown to enhance observed surface brightness of breaks in edge-on systems.
AI.conclusion: The high fraction of Type II breaks in edge-on galaxies is largely attributable to projection effects, which inflate break detectability; caution is needed when comparing break statistics across samples with different inclinations.

title: The Milky Way Atlas for Linear Filaments III: Giant filaments and magnetic fields as evidence of a bubbly Galactic disk
comment: 21 pages, 15 figures, 1 table, Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal
summary: Linear filamentary structures are fundamental constituents of the interstellar medium and play a central role in star formation. Their relative orientation with respect to the ambient magnetic field (B-field) provides key constraints on filament formation mechanisms. We investigate the relative orientation between Milky Way linear filaments (MWLFs) and the plane-of-sky B-field using polarization observations from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) DR6, complemented by Planck data. Filament orientations are compared with the local B-field and the Galactic plane, while projection effects and statistical significance are quantified using Monte Carlo simulations of vector pairs in three-dimensions. We find no strong preferential alignment between MWLFs and the ambient B-field. Although the B-field is preferentially aligned with the Galactic plane with relative angles $θ_{\rm BG} \sim0-25°$, filament orientations exhibit a bimodal distribution, being either parallel or perpendicular to the plane ($θ_{\rm FG} \sim0-15°$ and $\sim75-90°$). Filaments located far from the Galactic midplane ($|z|>90$ pc) preferentially show perpendicular alignment with both the plane and the B-field, whereas those near the midplane exhibit a bimodal orientation. These results indicate that large-scale B-fields do not dominate the formation of MWLFs and instead favor a super-Alfvénic regime in which magnetic forces are dynamically subdominant, as expected for filaments associated with supernova-driven shells. Overall, our findings suggest that a face-on view of the Milky Way would resemble nearby disk galaxies such as M74, as observed in JWST images, with its disk structured by a network of supernova-driven bubbles (i.e., a bubbly disk).

AI.tldr: Linear filaments in the Milky Way show no strong preferential alignment with the ambient magnetic field, exhibiting a bimodal orientation relative to the Galactic plane (parallel or perpendicular), and the data favor a super-Alfvénic (magnetically subdominant) regime, suggesting a "bubbly disk" structure driven by supernova shells.
AI.motivation: To constrain filament formation mechanisms by investigating the relative orientation between Milky Way linear filaments and the plane-of-sky magnetic field, which is a key observational diagnostic.
AI.method: Used ACT DR6 and Planck polarization data to compare filament orientations with local B-field and Galactic plane; quantified projection effects and statistical significance via Monte Carlo simulations of 3D vector pairs.
AI.result: No strong preferential alignment between filaments and B-field; B-field aligns with Galactic plane (θ_BG ~0-25°), but filaments show bimodal distribution relative to the plane (θ_FG ~0-15° and ~75-90°). Filaments far from the midplane (|z|>90 pc) are preferentially perpendicular to both plane and B-field; those near the midplane are bimodal.
AI.conclusion: Large-scale B-fields do not dominate filament formation; the data favor a super-Alfvénic regime where magnetic forces are dynamically subdominant, consistent with filaments formed by supernova-driven shells, implying a bubbly disk structure for the Milky Way similar to M74.

title: Bar-driven secular evolution largely complete in a disk galaxy 7.6 billion years ago
comment: Submitted. Comments and suggestions are very welcome
summary: Disk galaxies like the Milky Way are thought to evolve through internal dynamical processes: the stellar disk forms a bar, the bar drives gas inflow that builds a nuclear stellar disk, and the bar vertically thickens into an X-shaped bulge. Although this evolution is thought to be slow, completing only at late cosmic times, its timing remains poorly constrained. We report James Webb Space Telescope imaging of a galaxy at redshift 0.92 (7.6 billion years ago) that already hosts an X-shaped bulge, a nuclear stellar disk, and an extended stellar disk, with geometry and inferred bar size indistinguishable from those of present-day barred galaxies. The X-shaped bulge marks the completion of the major phase of bar-driven evolution when the Universe was less than half its current age.

AI.tldr: JWST imaging reveals a galaxy at redshift 0.92 (7.6 Gyr ago) already exhibiting an X-shaped bulge, nuclear stellar disk, and extended disk—structures indistinguishable from present-day barred galaxies—indicating that the major phase of bar-driven evolution completed when the Universe was less than half its current age.
AI.motivation: The timing of bar-driven evolution in disk galaxies (bar formation, gas inflow, X-shaped bulge thickening) remains poorly constrained; this work aims to determine when this process completes.
AI.method: JWST imaging observations of a galaxy at redshift 0.92, analyzing the morphology of its X-shaped bulge, nuclear stellar disk, and extended stellar disk, and comparing geometry and bar size to present-day barred galaxies.
AI.result: The galaxy at z=0.92 already hosts all structural components (X-shaped bulge, nuclear disk, extended disk) with geometry and bar size indistinguishable from local barred galaxies.
AI.conclusion: The major phase of bar-driven evolution can complete by z~0.9, when the Universe was less than half its current age, challenging the view that such evolution is slow and occurs only at late cosmic times.

title: Tilting at the Turnover: Modeling the Faint-End of the UV Luminosity Function Behind Abell s1063 with JWST
comment: 25 pages, 17 Figures, Submitting to MNRAS
summary: We leverage the strong gravitational field of Abell S1063 to identify faint, highly magnified galaxies using ultra-deep James Webb Space Telescope (JWST)/NIRCam imaging from the GLIMPSE survey and ancillary Hubble Space Telescope (HST)/ACS imaging from the Hubble Frontier Fields program. We construct a photometric catalogue of lensed high-redshift candidates and use these sources to constrain the faint end of the rest-frame UV luminosity function (UVLF) over $z\simeq6$--11. Rather than treating the UVLF turnover ($M_{\rm t}$) as a hard cutoff, we model it as a gradual quadratic suppression and explicitly account for the potential continued contribution of galaxies beyond the turnover. In a shallow-turnover scenario, up to one-third of the UV luminosity density can arise from sources fainter than $M_{\rm t}$. While we find no direct evidence for a turnover down to $M_{\rm UV}=-13.5$ at $z=6$, our analysis can only confidently exclude weak, medium, and strong turnover models down to $M_{\rm t}=-15.9$, $-15.1$, and $-14.8$, respectively. Across these models, we infer lower limits of the UV luminosity, star formation density, and the ionization rate as: $ρ_{\rm UV}\geq22\times10^{25}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}\,Hz^{-1}\,Mpc^{-3}}$, ${\rm SFRD}\geq25\times10^{-3}\,M_\odot\,{\rm yr^{-1}\,Mpc^{-3}}$, and $\log_{10}(\dot{n}_{\rm ion}/{\rm s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-3}})\geq51.02$. We find that galaxies fainter than the conventional $M_{\rm UV}=-17$ limit contribute more than half of the UV luminosity density and at least $\sim64\%$ of the ionizing photons produced by star-forming galaxies at $z=6$. Because our turnover model permits a suppressed, but non-zero, galaxy population beyond $M_{\rm t}$, sources fainter than the turnover remain contributors to both $ρ_{\rm UV}$ and $\dot{n}_{\rm ion}$, emphasizing the need to consider the turnover and its shape during reionization.

AI.tldr: Using JWST/NIRCam and HST/ACS imaging of Abell S1063, the study identifies faint, magnified high-redshift galaxies and models the UV luminosity function turnover as a gradual suppression rather than a hard cutoff. While no direct turnover is detected down to M_UV=-13.5 at z=6, the analysis constrains turnover models and shows that galaxies fainter than M_UV=-17 contribute >50% of UV luminosity density and ~64% of ionizing photons at z=6, with shallow-turnover scenarios allowing up to one-third of UV density from sources fainter than the turnover.
AI.motivation: To leverage gravitational lensing and ultra-deep JWST imaging to probe the faint end of the UV luminosity function at high redshift and constrain the nature of the UVLF turnover, which is critical for understanding galaxy formation and cosmic reionization.
AI.method: Used ultra-deep JWST/NIRCam imaging (GLIMPSE survey) and HST/ACS imaging (Hubble Frontier Fields) of the galaxy cluster Abell S1063; constructed a photometric catalogue of lensed high-redshift candidates; modeled the UVLF turnover as a gradual quadratic suppression rather than a hard cutoff; accounted for continued contribution of galaxies beyond the turnover; performed statistical analysis to constrain turnover strength and faint-end luminosity density.
AI.result: No direct evidence for a UVLF turnover down to M_UV=-13.5 at z=6; can exclude weak, medium, and strong turnover models down to M_t=-15.9, -15.1, and -14.8 respectively; inferred lower limits: ρ_UV≥22×10²⁵ erg s⁻¹ Hz⁻¹ Mpc⁻³, SFRD≥25×10⁻³ M⊙ yr⁻¹ Mpc⁻³, log₁₀(ṅ_ion/s⁻¹ Mpc⁻³)≥51.02; galaxies fainter than M_UV=-17 contribute >50% of UV luminosity and ~64% of ionizing photons at z=6; in shallow-turnover scenario, up to 1/3 of UV density comes from sources fainter than M_t.
AI.conclusion: The turnover shape matters significantly for reionization — a suppressed but non-zero galaxy population beyond the turnover continues to contribute to UV luminosity density and ionizing photon budget, emphasizing the need to consider both the turnover location and its functional form when modeling reionization.

title: Searching for the elusive CH2+ with the James Webb Space Telescope. Another carbocation to constrain astrochemical networks
comment: Accepted to A&A on the 16/06/2026
summary: Carbocations are key species in interstellar chemistry, providing entry points for building larger hydrocarbons. CH+, and more recently, CH3+, have been detected. Other carbocations await detection to provide a comprehensive view of the astrochemical network that is at work in the interstellar medium. We search for CH2+ in objects in which CH3+ was detected and evaluate the most favorable conditions for detecting the elusive CH2+ reactive cation. We calculated the CH2+ rotational and rovibrational transitions expected to contribute in the mid- to far-infrared, focusing on the lower-energy rovibrational levels. We then calculated CH2+ infrared emission spectra at different excitation temperatures and compared them to JWST spectra of the externally irradiated disk d203-506 in Orion, where CH+ and CH3+ have already been detected. We used thermochemical models to predict the abundance and spatial morphology of CH2+ to better understand its nondetection. The comparison to JWST spectra allowed us to provide excitation-temperature-dependent upper limits to the excited column density. These are several times lower than those detected for CH+ and CH3+ in their excited states. Based on model calculations for photodissociation regions and assuming similar excitation temperatures, the upper limit derived from observations and CH2+ model spectrum is either slightly above or below the column density expected from models of photodissociation regions. We provide a list of tabulated transitions to allow the community to search for this carbocation in future observations as CH2+ is key in providing observational constraints on astrochemical models.

AI.tldr: The paper searches for the elusive CH2+ carbocation in interstellar space using JWST observations, thermochemical models, and comparison with detected CH+ and CH3+, finding upper limits for its column density and providing transition tables for future searches.
AI.motivation: Carbocations like CH+, CH3+, and potentially CH2+ are key intermediates in interstellar hydrocarbon chemistry. Detecting CH2+ would complete the observational picture of the carbocation network in the interstellar medium and provide critical constraints on astrochemical models.
AI.method: Calculated CH2+ rotational and rovibrational transitions in mid- to far-infrared; computed infrared emission spectra at various excitation temperatures; compared to JWST spectra of the disk d203-506 in Orion where CH+ and CH3+ were detected; used thermochemical models to predict abundance and morphology; derived excitation-temperature-dependent upper limits on column density.
AI.result: CH2+ was not detected. Upper limits on excited column density are several times lower than those of CH+ and CH3+. The derived upper limits are either slightly above or below the column density predicted by photodissociation region models, depending on assumed excitation temperature.
AI.conclusion: CH2+ remains elusive but the upper limits help constrain astrochemical models. A tabulated list of transitions is provided to facilitate future searches for this key carbocation.
